Applying to the Chemistry Department
There are many different ways to join in and contribute to the fast-paced research
and innovation underway in the Chemistry Department at the University of Memphis.
Prospective Undergraduates
Students looking to complete an undergraduate degree as a B.S. or B.S.Ch. in Chemistry
at the University of Memphis may select and complete the appropriate application from
the listed forms on this page; more information including course listings and degree requirements can be found
in the University of Memphis catalog.
Prospective Graduate Students
Apply NOW at https://apply.memphis.edu/portal/graduate_application
Thank you in advance for your interest in the department -- we are very proud of our
current graduate students, faculty, and staff and look forward to learning how you
can contribute to the exciting discourse, research, and facilities underway in the
Chemistry Department. Before you join us however, you must submit an application.
Familiarize yourself with the application process by exploring the links below.
How to Apply to Graduate School >
Admission Requirements >
Application Forms, Prerequisites, and Policies >
Please note that teaching and research assistantships, including a competitive stipend
and all tuition and fees, are available only for full-time students on the doctoral
track (we even pay your parking!). Competition for assistantships is vigorous, and
there is no guarantee that all admitted students will receive financial assistance.
Once an assistantship has been awarded, funding is guaranteed for five years so long
as you are making satisfactory progress towards your degree. All students supported
on an assistantship are eligible for fully subsidized Health Insurance! For details,
see the Graduate School Health Insurance website.
All prospective graduate students must complete the application on the Graduate School
website to be considered for admission to Ph.D. and/or M.S. (Chemistry) courses of
study. Please note that students will not be allowed to enroll as a graduate student
in the Chemistry Department unless they meet the following prerequisites:
Satisfactory record of undergraduate coursework in chemistry
TOEFL (or equivalent) for most international applicants
Admission to Graduate School at the University of Memphis
* GRE examination is not required
Our application consists of:
Academic Transcripts
Personal Statement describing why you want to pursue an advanced degree in chemistry
at the University of Memphis
2 (minimum) Letters of Recommendation
International students must also supply the following:
Proof of English Language Proficiency: Ways to meet this foreign language requirement (TOEFL, Duolingo, etc.) can be found
on the graduate school admissions website.
Health Certificate: Within 30 days from the first day of classes, each international student must submit
a certificate from a licensed U.S. physician or other qualified U.S. medical authority
verifying freedom from tuberculosis.
Please see the graduate school's website for further information.
We accept applications for students wishing to start their degrees in either Fall
or Spring semesters. The priority application deadline for Fall admission is February
1. The priority application for Spring admission is July 1. We can accept applications after these dates (but before the Graduate School application
deadlines found on their website) until the class is full. Classes regularly fill
with applications received before the priority deadline. Prospective students are strongly encouraged to apply prior to these dates for full consideration.
For answers to frequently asked questions, visit our Frequently Asked Questions page.
Apply NOW at https://apply.memphis.edu/portal/graduate_application
NOTE: Please do not send application materials, including letters of recommendation,
directly to the Graduate Coordinator or any faculty member in chemistry. These materials
must be sent to the Graduate School. Your application can not be processed or considered
by the department until your application to the graduate school is complete. You do
not need a faculty sponsor to apply. Also, note that assistantships can not be approved until you are fully admitted to
the Graduate School via the application portal.
